# Does cracking your knuckles cause arthritis?

**Verdict:** 📚 Published evidence only

## Plain summary

The published evidence does not show that cracking your knuckles causes arthritis in the hands. [s18a7ea9d-effect, s8d3c1d17-effect] Multiple studies, including reviews and studies using hand X-rays, found no significant association between knuckle cracking and osteoarthritis. [s18a7ea9d-effect, s5c03da12-effect, s0f057a10-effect, sfc14bd95-effect] In one study, hand osteoarthritis was found in about 18 percent of habitual crackers and about 21 percent of non-crackers, a difference that was not statistically significant. [s0c90576d-effect, s10067ba6-effect] Some studies found no link between knuckle cracking and arthritis, swelling, or lower grip strength, while a few reported hand swelling or reduced grip strength in habitual crackers. [s1fb0d21b-effect, s3ce0fe8b-effect, s134aee18-effect, s8397b261-effect] Because the evidence is observational and certainty is low, this answer should be treated cautiously.

## Question (PECO)

- **Population:** adults who crack their knuckles regularly
- **Exposure:** regularly cracking one's knuckles, defined as doing so at least occasionally, typically by manually bending the fingers to produce a popping sound
- **Comparator:** not cracking knuckles
- **Outcome:** diagnosed osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis in the hands, as confirmed by clinical examination or imaging (e.g., X-ray)
- **Time window:** over the course of a lifetime
- **Estimand:** ATE, risk difference, deviations handled n/a

## Causal graph (DAG)

- knuckle_cracking → arthritis: the question being tested
- age → arthritis: cites s3956555d-design
- age → knuckle_cracking: assumed (no source)
- sex → arthritis: assumed (no source)
- sex → knuckle_cracking: assumed (no source)
- prior_joint_trauma → arthritis: cites s3956555d-design
- family_history_hand_oa → arthritis: cites s3956555d-design
- heavy_manual_labor → arthritis: cites s3956555d-design
- hand_swelling → arthritis: assumed (no source)
- knuckle_cracking → hand_swelling: cites s3ce0fe8b-effect, s134aee18-effect, s8397b261-effect
- grip_strength → arthritis: assumed (no source)
- knuckle_cracking → grip_strength: cites s3ce0fe8b-effect, s134aee18-effect, s8397b261-effect

Treated as exogenous (the model's judgment that nothing in the graph can cause it; no source): age, sex, prior_joint_trauma, family_history_hand_oa, heavy_manual_labor.

## Key confounders

- age
- sex

## Evidence

**Certainty:** low (starts low: best evidence is observational)

Evidence flow: 69 sources found → 50 studies after dedupe → 39 included (excluded: off_topic 7, not_a_study 3, wrong_population 1).

- [Let's get a hand on this: Review of the clinical anatomy of "knuckle cracking".](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30080300) — systematic_review, 2018: failed to show an association
- [Does knuckle popping lead to arthritis?](https://cdn.mdedge.com/files/s3fs-public/JFP06510725.PDF) — cross_sectional, year unknown: no significant association between crack years and OA (distal interphalangeal joint, mean 108 crack years; metacarpal phalangeal joint, mean 75 crack years)
- [Knuckle cracking and hand osteoarthritis.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21383216) — case_control, 2011: The prevalence of OA in any joint was similar among those who crack knuckles (18.1%) and those who do not (21.5%; P = .548)
- [Effects of habitual knuckle cracking on metacarpal cartilage thickness and grip strength.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2468122916301049) — cross_sectional, 2017: While habitual KC does not affect handgrip strength, it appears to be associated with increased MH cartilage thickness.
- [Study on the effects of cracking your knuckles](https://www.goldenstateortho.com/about/news-events/news/does-cracking-knuckles-cause-arthritis-no) — cross_sectional, 2015, known only from secondary sources: knuckle crackers did not show any hand problems from the practice; no link between knuckle cracking and arthritis, swelling, or lower grip strength; increased range of motion in knuckle crackers
- [Clinical Inquiry: Does knuckle popping lead to arthritis?](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27846331) — cross_sectional, 2016: Habitual knuckle popping, or cracking (over the course of several decades) isn't associated with clinical or radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis.
- [Effect of habitual knuckle cracking on hand function.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1004074) — cross_sectional, 1990: Habitual knuckle crackers were more likely to have hand swelling and lower grip strength. There was no increased preponderance of arthritis of the hand in either group
- [A 2011 study went further by removing the guesswork of self-diagnosis. Researchers reviewed hand X-rays from 215 adults aged 50 to 89 and compared radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis against each person’s knuckle-cracking history.](https://acibademinternational.com/blog/is-it-bad-to-crack-your-knuckles-the-60-year-experiment-that-answered-it) — cross_sectional, 2011, known only from secondary sources: no association between knuckle-cracking history and radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis
- [Does knuckle cracking lead to hand osteoarthritis?](https://highperformancept.nyc/library_newsfeed_125) — cross_sectional, 2011, known only from secondary sources: prevalence of KC among the controls was 23%, which was not significantly different from the prevalence in those with OA, which was 18%
- [Knuckle cracking: secondary hyperparathyroidism and what your mother did not tell you.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4438371) — case_control, 2013: no objective difference in the incidence of arthritis between the groups
- [No Association Between Knuckle Cracking and Osteoarthritis: A Cross-Sectional Study of 300 Adults Aged 45 and Older](https://acibademinternational.com/blog/does-cracking-your-knuckles-cause-arthritis) — cross_sectional, 1990, known only from secondary sources: No higher rate of hand arthritis in crackers than in non-crackers
- [Real-time visualization of joint cavitation.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4398549) — cross_sectional, 2015: the mechanism of joint cracking is related to cavity formation rather than bubble collapse
- [Evaluation of Students Self-Joint Cracking Habits: A Cross-Sectional Study](https://www.mevlanamedsci.org/pdf/evaluation-of-students-self-joint-cracking-habits-a-cross-sectional-study) — cross_sectional, year unknown: effect not verified
- [No significant correlation between knuckle-cracking and arthritis in a retrospective case-control study](https://www.news-medical.net/health/MythBusting-Does-Knuckle-Cracking-Really-Lead-to-Arthritis.aspx) — case_control, 2011, known only from secondary sources: no significant correlation between knuckle-cracking and arthritis, regardless of the frequency or duration of the habit
